reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in grass in 5-10 feet with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko and chatterbait. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with some fish on beds and a lot of bass fry in the back of pockets.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: South winds have slowed the schooling bass activity, but schooling action should improve throughout the lake within the next week as bass gorge on offshore shad. Some bass can still be caught in the reeds. Match the hatch with small profile baits like crappie launchers, clear topwaters, small Alabama rigs with small baits and small hard jerkbaits for offshore fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass and crappie good in creeks on minnows and small jigs. Largemouth bass are fair on soft plastics, spinnerbaits and crankbaits.
reports.by: Hundley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are stacking up in 13-30 feet of water on brush piles with the biggest fish on timber. Crappie are preferring minnows over jigs. Largemouth bass are post spawn and cruising points and structure. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Black bass are shallow in creeks and shallow banks. Fly fishing with craws and clouser minnow patterns should produce bass. Crappie and catfish are moving shallow fly fishing with wooly buggers, slow-sinking small fish patterns, or clouser minnows on sunny rocky shores might draw a strike. Crappie fishing has continued to be excellent, but this may change after the rain. Crappie are post spawn with more and more fish relating…
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on points around the shad spawn. Crappie fishing has continued to be excellent, but this may change after the rain. Crappie are post spawn with more and more fish relating to brush piles and timber.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are being caught inside weeds with dark colored plastics.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are scattered with the high water. Largemouth bass are fair on topwater baits fished around newly flooded cover. A slab or live bait fished around the main lake structure would be a good place to start.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8.01 pounds are slow in 5-15 feet of water all around the lake. Some bass are guarding fry and most are post spawn. Crappie are slow to 12 inches on jigs in 2-10 feet of water with a few spawning on the gravel flats.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass continue to be good cranking and slow dragging over rock.
reports.by: the Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing remains fair on brush in 10-20 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good on rock piles and shallow rocky points up with moving baits.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Some bass are spawning in the trees. Still some current in the river, so there are places the bass are trying to school up.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Some redfish being caught trolling out in front of the crappie wall on plastics and spoons. Channel catfish are being caught along rock lines blue catfish are slow bass no report.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Wind blown areas are stained, but still producing catches of bass.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing Tour

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, crappie and largemouth bass have been biting in 10-20 feet of water on the south and west sides of the lake.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are all over. Crappie are fair on structure 12-25 feet deep. Hybrids can be caught in 18-28 feet of water on flats and drop-offs with slabs, spoons, and live minnows or goldfish.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, with Bradley Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing has continued to be excellent, but this may change after the rain. Crappie are post spawn with more and more fish relating to brush piles and timber.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are stacking up in 13-30 feet of water on brush piles with the biggest fish on timber. Crappie are preferring minnows over jigs. Largemouth bass are post spawn and cruising points and structure. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Crappie fishing has continued to be excellent, but this may change after the rain. Crappie are post spawn with more and more fish relating to brush piles and timber.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Topwater bass action has begun. Solid 3-4 pound bass can be caught in 10-15 feet on points and ridges with shaky heads and Carolina rigs. Big bluegill can be caught on shaky heads while targeting bass.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Work topwaters over the bass guarding fry in the pockets. Black bass are post spawn and the top water bite is on! The crappie are moving shallow, small clousers are producing well. Crappie fishing is settling into the post spawn and summer patterns we should see for the next few months. We are seeing incredible numbers of small black crappie right now loading up on brush piles, lay downs, bridges and docks. The larger black crappie are a little hard to find but you can find some nice groups of them or pick a few out of the smaller fish. The bigger white crappie are beginning to load on the summer pattern trees. We have a tremendous amount of fry covering up a lot of those trees and making…
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in all stages of the spawn hitting creature baits and soft plastics. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs in shade and brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing remains consistent. Some bass are a bit deeper and a shaky head works wonders on this lake around offshore humps and ledges.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are excellent on slabs, spinnerbaits and spoons fished in 10-20 feet of water from near Blue Water Shores to Indian Harbor to the Shores in town. Largemouth bass continue to be good in the back of sloughs or near main lake points with soft plastics, jigs, spinnerbaits and lipless crankbaits. Crappie are good to excellent in the shallows on small jigs and small minnows fished under a cork.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on spinnerbaits fished in very shallow water in heavy cover. Crappie are very good on jigs fished in brush piles all over the lake. White bass are good on slab spoons fished along roadbeds and points.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: The best way to target white bass will be to cast slabs beneath the birds.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are eating well on trees and shallow structure. Crappie are tight to structure and need some enticing to eat but can be caught on small jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be pushing to deeper water with some male bass guarding fry. Crappie should be transitioning to brush piles biting jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good skipping docks with craws, flukes and worms, or cranking bulkheads and shallow rocks.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: There is a good early morning bass bite on topwaters around bushes and flooded grass. Shad spawn should begin soon, drawing bass near chunk rock, boat docks and hard-cover at daylight. Crappie are biting slip cork minnows on flooded cypress trees and vertical cover near the river.
reports.by: Brian Vickery Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good 10-15 feet of water with chartreuse jigs or minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good skipping docks with craws, flukes and worms, or cranking bulkheads and shallow rocks.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows in 10 feet of water on timber, concrete, and shallow brush piles. Largemouth bass can still be caught on beds, and docks with Texas rigs and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good skipping docks with craws, flukes and worms, or cranking bulkheads and shallow rocks.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with the best bite on Rosie red minnows near Sanford Yake area, off of the dock, and a few fish pulled out of Bugbee in the shallow areas. Minnows, bottom bouncers or floating worm harnesses, chartreuse, red mouth jerkbait or slab spoons are great choices.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on deep diving crankbaits, or Carolina rigs near creek channel swings. Crappie are fair on chartreuse and white crappie jigs on standing timber, smaller fish are on brush piles.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass are moving offshore stacking up and suspended 8 feet down over deeper water with a jerkbait. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on Carolina rigs, dropshots and medium paddle tail swimbaits. Crappie are fair on chartreuse and white crappie jigs on timber.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been good flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water. The spawn is ending and bass are staying in the shallows as the water temperature rises to the 80s. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Focus on holes in the reed banks where bass will set up on their beds. Watch for balls of bass fry because a fry guarder will be close by. Crappie were fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black Bass good, up to 12 lb. Some bass still spawning on deeper flats and points 6 to 15 ft. Crappie has been slow a few reports up River shallow on minnows.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The reports have been good to excellent on black bass. Crappie and white bass are good in the main lake area.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on Carolina rigs, small or big paddle tail swimbaits, and flukes. Crappie are fair on white crappie jigs or grubs in standing timber, with smaller fish on brush piles.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are slow to fair when you can find clear water with live shad or small white or silver slabs in 15-25 feet of water.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are related to brush piles 12-21 feet of water.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the post spawn pattern scattered from shallows and starting to congregate on brush for the summer pattern. Largemouth bass can be caught on grass with chatterbaits, weightless flukes, or white swim jigs. Dan’s Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan’s Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: A slab and jig combination is hard to beat, but the whites can be caught on any number of baits to include the MAL Lures, Mepps Spinners, and Lil' Georges. Crappie are slow with late spawning fish being caught on minnows in 2-4 feet of water in shallow water coves and off boat docks. Black bass are good and with the water level up it will put a lot of bass in the flooded grass. The shad will use the retaining walls and the dock poles to spawn on and the bass will be nearby.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Many bass are still shallow trying to spawn, but this should finish this week. Crappie and catfish are moving shallow and deep as they spawn. Some crappie are moving to brush but the bite is not steady yet.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina the crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets or worms, the catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. On the lake Crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-18 feet of water. Crappie are nearing the end of the spawn. Black bass are good on crankbaits and shiny spinnerbaits in 2-8 feet of water. Bass are nearing the end of the spawn.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: The black bass bite is improving steadily.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Water level is back to full pool, so this generally creates a tough bass and crappie bite.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Once the fish move out deeper, the silver, three-quarter ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab has been the ticket to later morning fish grouped up tightly, whereas using a sawtooth method of retrieve with the MAL Heavy is the go-to method for fish spread over a larger area. Largemouth bass are now consistently in 8-14 feet of water, especially on topographic irregularities with some form of cover present.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Hybrid stripers and white bass are good on artificial lures such as slab spoons and swimbaits. Crappie fishing is improving with a post spawn pattern in 8-12 feet on jigs and minnows. The largemouth bass bite is good on frogs and smaller trick baits and flukes.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass topwater action has finally started on yellow magics, spooks and buzz baits. There are some bass starting to make the way back off the bank in 10-14 feet of water hitting crankbaits and Texas rigged worms. Crappie are still fair in the creeks.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass and white bass are biting throughout the lake on bluff walls and creeks. Bass are good around docks and shallow grass with flukes, swimbaits and soft plastic worms.
reports.by: Randal Frisbee, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush piles with minnows and jigs in 12-16 feet of water. Bass are fair hitting crankbaits and plastic worms. Bass topwater bite improves daily. The big crappie and larger female bass are primarily post spawn, but you can find a few stragglers shallow. Bass are best on weightless flukes, crappie are best on minnows, catfish are great on prepared bait and nightcrawlers and the bream on best red worms and crickets.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush piles with minnows and jigs. Bass are fair on soft plastics in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 4-15 feet on jigs and minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 4-6 feet of water on minnows and jigs. White bass are moving up river with a good bite off points with slabs, and trolling crankbaits or rattle traps. Black bass are good on swimbaits, spinnerbaits, and topwater baits early in the morning. Some bass continue to be on beds with some males guarding fry in 8-12 feet of water. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 5-8 feet in grass with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senkos and chatterbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with some fish on beds and a lot of bass fry in the back of pockets. Bass continue to be good with most bass finished with the spawn on the mid to lower end. There is still some spawning bass on the upper end that can be caught with Texas-rigged plastic, or a big swimbait.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: There are still some bass in the reeds, but fish are post spawn and starting to push to deeper water. Match the hatch with small profile baits like crappie launchers, clear topwaters, small Alabama rigs with small baits and small hard jerkbaits for offshore fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in all stages of the spawn. Crappie can be caught on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie spawn is almost over pushing fish to roam offshore structure in 2-32 feet of water. Bass are primarily post spawn aggressively feeding. White bass are good with several limits reporting while trolling, and a few catches caught while fishing for crappie. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Black bass are shallow in creeks and shallow banks. Fly fishing with craws and clouser minnow patterns should produce bass. Crappie and catfish are moving shallow fly fishing with wooly buggers, slow-sinking small fish patterns, or clouser minnows on sunny rocky shores might draw a strike.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Shad spawns are key early morning to run numbers of bass up. DieZel chatterbaits and mini chatterbaits in white or Shad colors are best for bass in 1-3 feet. Crappie are excellent in full post spawn in the mouths of creeks leading to the main river channels.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good but scattered around docks and up shallow on the southern end. Largemouth bass good on Texas rigged plastics, jigs and pigs and topwater baits.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass up to 8.36 pounds are excellent in 1-5 feet of water all around the lake in spawning pockets on Hag’s Tornados in green pumpkin, Tsunami Jigs and White Outlier Frogs. Some bass are guarding fry and some are post spawn. Crappie are good to 10 inches on jigs in 2-10 feet with a few spawning on the gravel flats.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass continues to be good with a consistent bite pattern when around shad. Bass are being caught on main and secondary points, especially when targeting rock with crankbaits.
reports.by: the Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing remains fair on brush in 10-20 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with soft plastics and catfish are good with worms and minnows in 12 feet of water.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on the banks early and late in 1-20 feet of water on structure and bream beds during the day. Crappie have been pretty good on brush 8-25 feet of water. Hybrids can be caught in 17-29 feet of water on flats and drop-offs with slabs, spoons, and live minnows or goldfish.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, with Bradley Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in full post spawn patterns pushing off bank lines to roam in 5-15 feet on timber. The bite is excellent with crappie still preferring plastics over hand tied jigs or minnows.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie spawn is almost over pushing fish to roam offshore structure in 2-32 feet of water. Bass are primarily post spawn aggressively feeding. White bass are good with several limits reporting while trolling, and a few catches caught while fishing for crappie. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Crappie are excellent, roaming 8-35 feet of water full post spawn. Focus River channels for open water crappie and main lake bank lines sloping to the deeper parts, stacked on brush the next few weeks.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Some topwater bass action has begun. There is a good early shallow bite on under spins and rattle traps, then target bass in 10-15 feet on points and ridges on shaky heads and Carolina rigs.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been slow with some early morning catching near areas with the shad spawn using DieZel chatterbaits. Once bass move off the shore, switch to squarebill crankbaits in 3-5 feet, or Yum dingers and flukes around grass, and frogs in the grass. Black bass are post spawn and the top water bite is on! The crappie are moving shallow, small clousers are producing well. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork is moving rapidly into the post spawn pattern.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing remains consistent. Some bass are a bit deeper and a shaky head works wonders on this lake around off shore humps and ledges.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Bouncing a slab or spoon will put sandbass in the boat. Crappie continue to be good in the backs of creeks on small minnows and jigs. Largemouth bass are also good on soft plastics, lipless crankbaits and spinnerbaits in the shallows on most every creek and slough.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on spinnerbaits fished in shallow water in areas where the shad are spawning. Crappie are fair on jigs fished in brush piles.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greenbelt fishing report
reports.text: Few reports of crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Chain Pickerel and black bass are spawning in shallow water. Look for spawning crappie in weeds on sloping banks.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass will be snapping in these areas eating frogs, lipless crankbaits and grubs Texas rigged.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing remains consistent. Target bass in grass patches and work the area over with worms or creature baits. Look for deeper ledges and rock piles for some of those special sized bass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting soft plastics and swimbaits shallow, and out on brush piles. A lot of bass are now suspended in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught flipping soft plastics into the bushes, or working the outside edges of willows with 10 inch worms or any bait that puts off a lot of action. Shad spawn should begin soon, drawing bass near chunk rock, boat docks and hard cover at daylight. Crappie are biting slip cork minnows on flooded cypress trees and vertical cover near the river.
reports.by: Brian Vickery Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good 10-15 feet of water with chartreuse jigs or minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good on flats, brush, rock piles or along bulkheads with shallow crankbaits, spinnerbaits, flukes and soft plastics like worms or creature baits.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair to good on points and humps in 15-30 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are slow to fair in 2-24 feet of water on brush piles, submerged timber, and submerged cover near drop-offs with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: White bass are great in 6-15 feet of water on wind blown points and ledges with white and chartreuse slabs.
reports.by: Michael Richardson, Lake Livingston Adventures

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Bass patterns are consistent. Target bass in grass patches and work the area over with worms or creature baits. Look for deeper ledges and rock piles for some of those special sized bass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on swimbaits, bladed jigs and redbug Texas rigged worms fishing the hydrilla out to 10 feet. Crappie are good suspended in brush piles in 25 feet of water with minnows and 3 inch pintail jigs.
reports.by: Hambone guide service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good using chartreuse jigs and rosie red minnows fished in Sanford Yake area, off of the dock, and a few fish pulled out of Bugbee in the shallow areas. Minnows, bottom bouncers or floating worm harnesses, chartreuse, red mouth jerkbait or slab spoons are great choices.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millers Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have improved to fair in 3-4 feet of water. Black bass are slow on main lake points with soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on Carolina rigged plum or blue flecked worms in 12 feet of water on grass lines. Crappie are fair on chartreuse and white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Prior to the weekend rain, bass were stacking up in suspended mode 8 feet down over deeper water with a jerkbait. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on Carolina rigged plum or blue flecked worms in 12 feet of water on grass lines. Crappie are fair on chartreuse and white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 12 pounds possible. Soft imitation shad or crappie plastic baits on a Shaky Head or wobble head have been working on beds. Crappie are slow with few catches to report.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good on brush piles in 12-15 feet of water around docks. Bass are fair around shallow cover.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting in deep water biting on minnows.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on medium diving crankbaits. Crappie are good on a clear or white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair when you can find clear water with live shad or small white or silver slabs in 15-25 feet of water.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be caught in shallow water on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are relating to brush piles in 12-21 feet of water.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still in all stages of the spawn from 3-20 feet of water shad imitation baits. crappie will be moving to brush. Some largemouth bass are on spawning beds. Largemouth bass continue to stage on secondary points hitting slow moving swimbaits, or along grass edges with chatterbaits. Dan’s Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan’s Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: A slab and jig combination is hard to beat, but the whites can be caught on any number of baits to include the MAL Lures, Mepps Spinners, and Lil' Georges. Crappie are fair with spawning fish being caught in 2-4 feet of water in the Richland and Chambers Creek tributaries, shallow water coves and off boat docks with minnows. Black bass are good in shallow was as some are still spawning while others are guarding fry. Shad will spread out on the points, and this is a great opportunity to catch bass with shallow crankbaits.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and catfish are moving shallow and deep as they spawn.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina the crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets or worms, the catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. On the lake Crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-18 feet of water. Crappie are spawning. Black bass are good on crankbaits and shiny spinnerbaits in 2-8 feet of water. Bass are nearing the end of the spawn.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on shallow remote rocky banks with soft plastics. Crappie are fair in mid depths on docks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Once the fish move out deeper, the silver, three-quarter ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab has been the ticket to later morning fish. Dropping the slab to the bottom and cranking it smoothly and consistently 5 to 6 turns up off the bottom while observing for fish response on 2-D sonar or forward facing soar is the key to getting bit consistently. Largemouth bass are now consistently in 8-14 feet of water, especially on topographic irregularities with some form of cover present.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still scattered and in spawning stages. Bass are at the backs of coves and for suspended fish near docks.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: There are still numbers of bass on the bank in 1-5 feet biting wacky worms and senko. A few bass are starting to move out to 6-12 feet hitting Carolina rigs, Texas rigs and mid running crankbaits. Crappie action is finally picking up in 5-9 feet of water, shallow timber, brush piles and shallow docks with jigs.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Conditions on the main lake are tough for bass fishing due to clear water, blue skies and the lack of wind. Bass are tucked into shaded spots out of the sun and sight of predators. Some bass can be caught along the grass with swimbaits. Downsize baits and slow your approach dragging small Ned rigs dragging slowly to catch 2-3 pound bass. Some bass are still on spawning beds. Largemouth are great in the shallow grass near the inside grass line.
reports.by: Randal Frisbee, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush piles with minnows and jigs in 12-16 feet of water. Bass are fair hitting crankbaits and plastic worms. Bass and crappie are being caught in good numbers all over the lakes. Many bass are actively spawning with weightless plastics or Texas rigs working well right now. Crappie are being caught shallow in grass and in 5-10 feet as different waves of fish move in and out from spawning.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are nearing the end of the spawn with half the fish being caught post spawn. Crappie are on good from 18 inches along the banks out to 3 feet and spawned out fish are in 12 feet of water in the creeks and channels hitting blue and chartreuse jigs or minnows. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good spawning as shallow as 1 foot on the rocks. Bass are fair along shallow banks spawning on beds hitting plastics and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good 2-12 feet on jigs and minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Black bass are good on swimbaits, spinnerbaits, and topwater baits early in the morning.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with fish in all stages of spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 5-8 feet of water in grass with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko and chatterbait. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with a lot of fish biting shallow in the mornings. Bass are guarding shallow fry, and there are still plenty of fish on beds. Lake Austin is good for bass. Most bass are done spawning on the mid to lower end. There is still some spawning bass on the upper end, so use Texas-rigged plastics there.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Big numbers of bass can be caught which is typical for spring on Bastrop. Some bass are still stacked up in the reeds hitting Texas rigs, but fish are primarily spawned out hitting wacky worms in the submerged grass just outside of the reeds. As the water temperature rises to 80 degrees, bass will seek the thermocline and start schooling.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: The go to artificial is the silver �¾ ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab, especially if most of the fish are on the small size, under 11 inches.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be in all stages of the spawn. Crappie and white bass should be in the creeks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on natural colored Texas rigged creature baits and wacky rigs. Black bass are shallow in creeks and shallow banks. Fly fishing with craws and clouser minnow patterns should produce bass. Crappie and catfish are moving shallow fly fishing with wooly buggers, slow-sinking small fish patterns, or clouser minnows on sunny rocky shores might draw a strike.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are moving up to the 2-4 feet on flats with a good bite on flukes, wacky worms, spinnerbaits and chatterbaits in 2-4 feet. Crappie are fair as fish transition to a post spawn pattern.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the middle of their spawn, especially in the southern end of the lake. Check out quiet coves and bays for spawning largemouth bass using soft plastics and jigs for bedding fish.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 7.57 pounds are excellent in 1-5 feet of water all around the lake in spawning pockets on Hag’s Tornados, cheat codes in white or green pumpkin, glides baits and Outlier Frogs. Crappie are good to 11 inches on jigs in 2-10 feet starting to move shallow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Following the recent cold front, the bite on Lake Bryan has improved and bass are becoming more active. Bass are being caught on main and secondary points, especially when targeting rock with crankbaits.
reports.by: the Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush in 10-20 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Start fishing for bass in shallow flooded grass, bushes or small trees with a frog or a fluke. If there are no grass mats, try trees that would be in the 2-3 foot depth at normal pool as the bass may pull out and hold tight to the trees when the lake falls.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent with fish in all stages of the spawn.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing Tour

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Reports of great catches using silver or white slabs and spinnerbaits with a very slow retrieve off the bottom in 17-26 feet of water. The crappie have also migrated back into the main lake.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in shallow water with minnows. Bass are good in deeper water hitting soft plastic worms.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good as most have moved off the beds and are ready to eat. Crappie have been good on minnows and jigs on structure. Hybrids are now back to jigging or slab, spoons, live bait, large goldfish or large minnows on flats and drop-offs in 17-26 feet of water.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, with Bradley Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good 1-15 feet of water in timber with plastics over hand tied jigs or minnows.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Corpus Christi Lake fishing report
reports.text: Reports from local anglers are slow for bass, catfish are fair and alligator gar are good.
reports.by: Weber’s Boat Landing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on natural colored Texas rigged creature baits and wacky rigs. Crappie are excellent with most fish post spawn. Crappie are moving to brush, but the majority are roaming in 5-35 feet of water in the river channels.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are great in 3-15 feet of water on hard bottoms with crankbaits, senkos or power worms. Crappie are slow with fish scattered.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: There is a good early shallow bite on under spins and rattletraps, then target bass in 10-16 feet for a slow bite on shaky heads and Carolina rigs. It has been too windy for topwater bass action, and with forecasted high winds this may not change.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass and shad are spawning. Shallow water seems to be best for bass in 1-4 feet using chatterbaits, flukes and Yum Dingers. Texas rigs are catching bass at the edge of grass with creature baits and beavers 1-3 feet. Black bass are shallow, fish warm windy banks. The crappie are moving shallow, small clouser minnows are producing well. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork has been a bit tougher this spring.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in all stages of the spawn hitting creature baits and soft plastics. Crappie can be good with minnows or jigs in shade and brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Lake Georgetown is fishing good for bass. Some bass are a bit deeper and a shaky head works wonders on this lake around off shore humps and ledges.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are up in shallow water in the creek with minnows and jigs. Bass are moving up in shallow water feeding on shad.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass action is excellent on chartreuse and white slabs fished in 13-18 feet of water on many areas of the lake. Black bass anglers are catching some good fish to 8 pounds on the lower ends and upstream above the 377 business bridge on lipless crankbaits and soft plastics. Many of the largemouth bass and crappie are in the back of the creeks spawning. Crappie are good on small minnows and small jigs fished under a cork.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on spinnerbaits and chatterbaits fished in shallow cover. Crappie are good in shallow water and are moving to open lake brush piles.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Cast towards the bank with slabs and jigging spoons and then reel back to the boat.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greenbelt fishing report
reports.text: Reports of anglers targeting crappie and bass with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Small bass are active in shallow areas relating to vegetation and structure. Look for spawning crappie in weeds on sloping banks.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are snapping in the shallows and drop offs eating grubs, spinnerbaits and starting to hit a few frogs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with primarily smaller sized fish up to 3 pounds. Crappie are good under docks hitting minnows or jigs. A bass was caught while targeting crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Target bass in grass patches and work the area over with worms or creature baits. Look for deeper ledges and rock piles for some of those special sized bass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good shallow and off of docks on soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on natural colored Texas rigged creature baits and wacky rigs.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good 10-15 feet of water with chartreuse jigs or minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Target bass in grass patches and work the area over with worms or creature baits. Look for deeper ledges and rock piles for some of those special sized bass.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on points and humps in 15-30 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are slow to fair in 2-24 feet of water on brush piles, submerged timber, and submerged cover near a drop-offs with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 10 feet of water on brush. Largemouth bass are in 4 feet or less on Texas rigs and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Catching white bass in 6-15 feet of water on wind blown points and ledges with white and chartreuse slabs.
reports.by: Michael Richardson, Lake Livingston Adventures

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Target bass in grass patches and work the area over with worms or creature baits. Look for deeper ledges and rock piles for some of those special sized bass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good fishing the hydrilla with swimbaits, chatterbaits and Texas rigged worms. Crappie are good in 20-25 feet fishing brush piles and timber with minnows and 3 inch pintail jigs. Catfish are good fishing under crappie schools with live bait.
reports.by: Hambone guide service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent in shallow water on chartreuse and white ⅜ ounce bladed jigs. Crappie are fair in standing timber and small brush piles leading into creeks.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with a fluke around the spawning grounds. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are good with topwater poppers or a white swim jig in shallow water. Crappie are fair in shallow brush or timber with white and chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been good flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water. The spawn is starting up and bass are beginning to flood the shallows. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Focus on holes in the reed banks where bass will set up on their beds. Crappie were fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 12 pounds on shad imitation soft plastics in 4-15 feet primarily around the salt cedar points and back of brushy coves. Crappie are scattered with very few reports. Some crappie are being caught up The Colorado River around Rocky shallow flats.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass bite is improving in shallow water on reaction baits like bladed jigs and shallow running crankbaits.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Black bass, hybrids and sand bass are slow.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good up shallow with a dropshot and light Carolina rigs with straight tail worms or ribbon tails. Crappie slow on a clear with black speckle on an ⅛ ounce crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair stg live shad or small white or silver slabs in 15-25 feet of water.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Reports of crappie biting in shallow water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Small roadrunner type baits and small crappie jigs are catching fish. Crappie are good with numbers showing up in the creeks and shallow water especially on sunny days that warm the shallow water.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: A few post spawn crappie are in 6-12 feet of water on brush piles, and many are spawning or staging right outside of the spawning areas. Target crappie with black and chartreuse, white and chartreuse, or orange and chartreuse jigs or minnows. Some largemouth bass are on spawning beds. Largemouth bass continue to stage on secondary points hitting slow moving swimbaits, or along grass edges with chatterbaits. Dan’s Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan’s Crappie Co

reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: The shallow bass bite is tough after the cold front and dropping water levels. Crappie and catfish are moving shallow and deep as they spawn.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina the crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets or worms, the catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. On the lake crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-18 feet of water. Crappie are prespawn and full of eggs. Black bass are good on crankbaits and shiny spinnerbaits in 2-8 feet of water. Bass are nearing the end of the spawn.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair slowly flipping plastic worms in less than a foot of water in the gap behind the cattails. Crappie are fair in mid depths on docks. Catfish are good at night, with several caught when targeting crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: The go to artificial is the silver �¾ ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab, especially if most of the fish are on the small size under 11 inches.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Hybrid striper and white bass are good on artificial lures such as slab spoons and smaller swimbaits. Crappie are improving better. Largemouth bass are very good on buck brush in 1-4 feet of water with senkos and wacky rigged smaller flukes.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Catfish are good, and crappie are slow throughout the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are scattered in the creeks as they spawn and wrap up spawning. Bass fishing will improve with the stained water and rise in lake levels.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with reported catches up to 9 pounds. While the water remains high the bass are staying shallow in 1-7 feet of water. Crappie are still hit-and-miss with a few showing up on shallow brush piles and some in the creeks.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good all day on deep bluff walls with craw baits. Edges of grass will produce bass with tiny swimbaits. Lake Travis is producing lots of bass right now. Lots of bass are piling up in numbers on the flats, especially ones with grass on the mid to lower end. Use your soft plastics and moving boats like swimbaits, shallow crankbaits and jerkbaits for these bass. We are catching lots of bass from 2-6 pounds with a few bigger ones mixed in.
reports.by: Randal Frisbee, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush piles with minnows and jigs. Bass fishing has slowed to fair as bass transition to post spawn patterns hitting crankbaits and plastic worms. Bass and crappie are being caught in good numbers all over the lakes. Many bass are actively spawning with weightless plastics or Texas rigs working well right now. Crappie are being caught shallow in grass and in 5-10 feet as different waves of fish move in and out from spawning.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on fire from 18 inches along the banks out to 12 feet in the creeks and channels hitting jigs or minnows. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are spawning as shallow as 1 foot on the rocks. Bass are fair along shallow banks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are up the river spawning. White bass fishing is good on slabs in 25-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass fishing is good using soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be shallow on spawning beds, and post spawn or staging in deeper water near spawning areas hitting soft plastics. Crappie should be spawning or staged on brush in 8-12 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush in 3-18 feet on jigs and minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Post spawn bass are on secondary points in 8-15 feet of water with slow moving plastics. Some bass are still spawning on shallow beds. Report by Kurt Dove, Pro Bass Guide.
reports.by: Kurt Dove, Pro Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are being caught off the piers at the state park and around bridges.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good and can be caught in grass 5-8 feet with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko and chatterbait. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: The 3/4 ounce silver Bladed Hazy Eye slab works best for fish directly under the boat, and the MAL Heavy with silver blade and chartreuse tail works well when fish are out away from the boat. The live shad bite is starting to warm up for white bass, largemouth bass, hybrid striped bass, and blue catfish are biting on shad presented on a Carolina rig terminated with a Kahle or circle hook.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good overall. Expect more bass on beds once water conditions stabilize. Black bass are shallow in creeks and shallow banks. Fly fishing with craws and clouser minnow patterns should produce bass. Crappie and catfish are moving shallow fly fishing with wooly buggers, slow-sinking small fish patterns, or clouser minnows on sunny rocky shores might draw a strike.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on main lake points and flats with chatterbaits and spinnerbaits. Bass are good with Texas rigs on big bushes and standing timber near spawning areas and flats or pond dams in 3-5 feet of water.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: It is possible to catch crappie and bass from the crappie house and from the bank.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass were good in the weeds on plastics.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, soft plastics and crankbaits will put them in the boat. The crappie spawn is in full swing. Largemouth bass are also into their spawn.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8.50 pounds are excellent in 1-5 feet of water all around the lake in spawning pockets on Hag’s Tornados, cheat codes in white or green pumpkin, glides baits and Outlier Frogs. Crappie are good to 11 inches on jigs in 2-10 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: The recent front has moved bass around, but fish can still be found in grass lines with wacky rigs and Texas rigs. Bass are very good around grass in 6-12 feet of water with swimbaits, crankbaits and chatterbaits. Topwater bite should kick off for bass and stripers as the shad spawn kickoffs.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing Tour

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been up on beds this past week and sight fishing was good. Crappie are fair to good in the shallows to 25 feet around structure or timber using jigs. Hybrids are now back to jigging or slab, spoons, live bait, large goldfish or large minnows on flats and drop-offs in 8-24 feet of water.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, with Bradley Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good overall. Expect more bass on beds once water conditions stabilize. Crappie are excellent from 10 inches to 20 feet of water. Crappie jigs are out producing minnows and hand ties.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with chatterbaits and spinnerbait round spawning flats and secondary points in 1-4 feet of water. Black bass are shallow, fish warm windy banks.Top water bite is on! The crappie are moving shallow, small clouser minnows are producing well. Lake Fork crappie fishing has been super up and down just like the weather has been. Crappie are scattered in 2-40 feet biting swimbaits, minnows, hand tied jigs and soft plastics.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in all stages of the spawn hitting creature baits and soft plastics. Crappie are good with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are close to their spawning grounds and are good on soft plastics and spinnerbaits. Crappie are also in the back of creeks and sloughs and are good on small white/,blue and black jigs or just use a small minnow. Best bait is a white and chartreuse slab bounced off the bottom near humps and ridges in 13-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: The late spring pattern of targeting the tops of humps with slabs, and working birds should be begin soon.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Small bass are active in shallow areas relating to vegetation and structure. Look for spawning crappie in weeds on

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are snapping in the cedar trees and laydowns eating small worms, grubs, spinnerbaits and swimbaits. Crappie can be enticed on brush piles deep and a few still in the shallows eating minnows and small jigs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with primarily smaller sized fish. Target bass in shallow water with bladed jigs and spinnerbaits. Crappie are good with reports of big females under docks hitting minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Inks Lake is fishing well for bass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water on soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good overall. Expect more bass on beds once water conditions stabilize.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Lake LBJ is fishing good for bass. Bass are very good around grass with crankbaits and flukes, or on brush piles in 8-12 feet of water with Texas rig and a crankbait. Bass are still spawning in the canals, with many bedding fish for anglers that want to sight fish.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on points and humps in 15-30 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 2-24 feet of water with minnows or jigs.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: The pier at Lake Limestone Marina and Campground has been exceptionally good while crappie travel to and from spawning areas. Largemouth bass are in 4 feet or less on Texas rig and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with jerkbaits, lipless crankbaits, walking topwater baits and Texas rigged worms. Crappie have been good in 15-25 feet suspended over brush using minnows and 3 inch soft plastic jigs. Sand bass remain good around the discharge area on small underspin jigs and slab spoons.
reports.by: Hambone guide service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good using Chartreuse jigs and minnows fished in Sanford Yake area, off of the dock, and a few fish pulled out of Bugbee in the shallow areas. Minnows, bottom bouncers or floating worm harnesses, chartreuse, red mouth jerkbait or slab spoons are great choices.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent in shallow water on bladed jigs, shallow diving crankbaits and lightly weighted Texas rigged craws. Crappie are excellent on flooded timber in 15-20 feet of water suspended just under the surface in 4 feet of water.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: The majority of bass were caught with a fluke around the spawning grounds. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent with senkos, stick baits, finesse worms, and wacky rigged worms. Crappie are fair with chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Most anglers are targeting crappie in shallow water and brush piles with minnows. Few reports of white bass, catfish and largemouth bass.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good with catches up to 13 pounds with one 16 pounder caught this last week. Crappie are starting to pick up with a few being reported up The Colorado River on minnows and red chartreuse 1/16 ounce jigs.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in deep water, but should move shallow as the weather warms.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair on shallow swimbaits, paddle tail swimbaits. Crappie slow on a white crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Small roadrunner type baits and small crappie jigs working. Crappie are hood and numbers are showing up in the creeks and shallow water especially sunny days that warms the shallow water.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are staging on secondary points hitting slow moving swimbaits, or along grass edges with chatterbaits. Dan’s Crappie Co. Crappie are good in 10-18 feet of water on trees in the creek channels. Targeting prespawn staging crappie.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan’s Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good in 20 feet of water on main lake points, roadbeds, and humps using a slab and jig combination. Crappie being caught on minnows in 2-4 feet of water on the Richland and Chambers Creek tributaries, and in shallow water coves and off boat docks.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
