reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina the crappie bite is good, bluegill are fair on crickets or worms, the catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. On the lake crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-18 feet of water. Crappie are prespawn and full of eggs and close to spawning. Black bass are good on crankbaits and spinnerbaits in 2-8 feet of water. Bass are spawning.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with males pushing shallow out to 3 feet of water staging on rocks near the dam and cattails. Cast soft plastics worms and creature baits on a heavy line, basically rig anything weedless to target bass in the cattails. Crappie are good in shallow water. Still not seeing big female crappie but the spawn should be around the corner. Catfish are good at night, with several caught when targeting crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: The 3/4 ounce silver Bladed Hazy Eye slab works best for white bass directly under the boat in 35 feet of water, and the MAL Heavy with silver blade and chartreuse tail works well when fish are out away from the boat from 10-25 feet.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, swim baits and crappie jigs are putting fish in the boat. Crappie are about a week away from turning on. The largemouth spawn has kicked into high gear.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Catfish and crappie are reported to be good.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Look for crappie in the creeks with inflow and watch the rising water temps this week. Largemouth and smallmouth bass fishing is picking up. The slab bite will start soon.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 1-6 feet of water with frogs, wacky worms, senkos, and Texas rig lizards. If the lake continues to rise, the bass will go to the flooded bushes. Crappie fishing has slowed while the creeks are muddy, but as the water clears road runners and tube jigs with 1/16 ounce heads.will be productive.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass have moved up on beds and they are hungry. Fish the coves and cuts, and there is a lot of bass out on the grass flats.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good spawning in shallow water and staging in 12 feet of water on brush piles with minnows and jigs. Bass are good in shallow water and in 12 feet of water with crankbaits and plastic worms. Bass and crappie are being caught in good numbers all over the lakes. Many bass are actively spawning with weightless plastics or Texas rigs working well right now. Crappie are being caught shallow in grass and in 5-10 feet as different waves of fish move in and out from spawning.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good 5-25 feet on jigs and minnows fished near structure.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 5-10 feet of water in the first drop-off zone with soft plastics. Bedding bass are in 6-8 feet of water. Report by Kurt Dove, Pro Bass Guide.
reports.by: Kurt Dove, Pro Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, crappie and bass will follow the shad into the shallows.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in grass in 5-12 feet with Texas rigged worms, wacky rig senko and chatterbait. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning with a lot of shallow fish.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Some bass are still stacked up in the reeds hitting Texas rigs, but fish are primarily spawned out hitting wacky worms in the submerged grass just outside of the reeds. As the water temperature rise to 80 degrees, bass will seek the thermocline and start schooling.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: After the morning spawning is over, move out to 20-34 feet and use silver, 3/4 ounce Hazy Eye Slabs with forward facing sonar in downward mode to catch fish later in the morning or just before sunset.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The lake is low and the bass bite has been really good with fish moving into spawning areas and flats and shallow points. The predicted rain may slow the crappie bite with an influx of water from the creeks. Expect crappie to be scattered in deep water.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving shallow to spawn. Slabs, soft plastics and crankbaits will put them in the boat. Largemouth bass are also moving in to spawn.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 10.19 pounds are excellent in 1-5 feet of water all around the lake in pockets on Hag’s Tornados, cheat codes in white or green pumpkin, glide baits, jerkbaits. Bass are in all stages of the spawn. Crappie are good to 12 inches on jigs in 5-10 feet of water pushing shallow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 7-15 feet with chartreuse jigs. Crappie pattern is consistent with fish in all stages of the spawn. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are very good on points with crankbaits, topwater lures, or dragging a Carolina rigged fluke. Bass can be caught along the rocks in these areas with chatterbaits or crankbaits. Crappie are on brush piles in 12-18 feet of water with minnows.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Lots of big bass being caught around the trees, with reports of several fish over 10 pounds.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in all stages of the spawn. As the water temperature increases the bass will become more aggressive. Bass are very good around grass in 6-12 feet of water with swimbaits, crankbaits and chatterbaits. Topwater bite should kick off for bass and stripers as the shad spawn kickoffs.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing Tour

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 10 feet of water hitting soft plastic worms. Crappie are transitioning shallow off docks in 10-20 feet of water with minnows.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is consistent on soft plastic lizards and craw worms in 2-7 feet of water on reeds and stumps.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are bedding, with some nice catches possible sight fishing.The biggest report is that the shad have started moving on the bulkheads in a scattered fashion. Crappie are fair to good in the shallows to 18 feet around structure or timber using jigs. Hybrids are now back to jigging or slab, spoons, live bait, large goldfish or large minnows on flats and drop-offs in 8-23 feet of water.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, with Bradley Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Expect the crappie bite to slow due to the rain in the forecast. Influx of water in the main lake from the creeks will raise the water level and muddy the clarity and scatter crappie.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in 25 feet of water on live minnows. Bass are excellent in a post spawn pattern, cast big crankbaits or Texas rig power worms to 8 feet of water.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Some topwater bass action. Bigger bass are spawned out hitting shaky head worms in 6-8 feet of water. Some bass are still shallow spawning along the banks.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been good most days with a better bite late in the evening. Lots of spawning bass all over the lake. Lake Fork crappie fishing has been steady with numbers of big fish possible when the winds allow. Good numbers of crappie on timber in 6-20 feet close to spawning areas. Wind directions and wind speeds are dictating a lot of the crappie’s location and demeanor.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good moving shallow to feed on shad. Crappie are heading up the creek about to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are moving to the spawning beds in shallower water and are good on soft plastics, lipless crankbaits and spinnerbaits. The crappies are also in the shallows and are good on small jigs fished under a float. Sand bass are good on numerous areas of the lake with slabs bounced off the bottom on humps. Many sand bass and crappie are in the river near Tin Top as well.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on jigs and spinnerbaits fished in very shallow water. Crappie are good in shallow water all over the lake and some are moving to main lake brush piles.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Schools of white bass are on the edges of humps in 22-25 feet of water with �¾-1 ounce slabs with a stinger hook.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greenbelt fishing report
reports.text: Reports of anglers targeting crappie with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are in the shallows eating chatterbaits, frogs and spinnerbaits. Crappie are decent in Luces Bayou eating small jigs very close to brush piles.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be shallow on spawning beds hitting soft plastics and creature baits. Post spawn bass should be in 8-12 feet of water hitting Carolina rigs or crankbaits. Crappie should be shallow or on brush piles be caught with jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good for numbers but not for size. Target bass in shallow water with bladed jigs and spinnerbaits. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good along the banks and just off the bank with soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: The big bass are shallow on beds, or waiting just off the bank to move shallow. Crappie are on shallow timber hitting jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: The crappie spawn started over a week ago, but is still not in the height of the spawn. Crappie catches in 1-12 feet of water targeting the base of button willows with jigs. Some female crappie are suspended around timber outside the spawning grounds. Black bass are in the creek systems, guarding nests, and in the back of the coves along with the crappie. Target bass are good early morning in 1-5 feet of water casting a white and chartreuse spinnerbaits to the bank then reel it slowly back to the boat. The rest of the day target bass from the bank to 7 feet around submerged button willows or shallow timber with a Texas rig, darker color worms, or senko.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 10-15 feet of water on brush with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Many bass are on or around beds with this first wave of spawn. Bass are very good around grass with crankbaits and flukes, or on brush piles in 8-12 feet of water with Texas rig and a crankbait. Bass are still spawning in the canals, with many bedding fish for anglers that want to sight fish.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are slow to fair in or near river channels and on points and humps in 18-40 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are fair with minnows and jigs in 2-30 feet of water on brush piles, submerged timber, and submerged cover close to a drop off ledge. Largemouth bass are staging around spawning pockets in 4-10 feet of water. Crappie are still on deep brush and trees in 20 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: There should be a few more weeks of good bank fishing for bass and crappie, especially off docks. A few crappie are transitioning back out to brush, but can still be caught in the creeks. Largemouth bass are in 4 feet or less on Texas rig and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on walking baits, jerkbaits, underspin swimbaits and Texas rigged junebug worms. Crappie are good in brush piles in 10-20 feet on minnows. Large catfish are good around brush holding brim and crappie with live bait. Sand bass are good in the discharge area using slab spoons and �¼ ounce roadrunners.
reports.by: Hambone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: The majority of bass were caught with a fluke around the spawning grounds. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent with shallow Carolina rigs, or shallow paddle tail swimbaits. Crappie are fair with chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great shallow near the boats, and on brush piles with black and chartreuse jigs or minnows. Largemouth bass.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Main lake bass are very good to 14 pounds on a variety of baits. Live scoping main lake points in 8-17 feet for bass with a variety of creature baits and shad imitation soft plastics. Crappie are still slow but a few are being caught shallow up The Colorado River on live bait.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie still have not moved shallow to spawn. Black bass are slow.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: The bass are working the shallows with 10-12 inch worms along the edge of the hydrilla and water lines. Chatterbaits, dropshots, and wacky rigs are a good set of bait options for anglers seeking to join in on the bass fishing. No reports of crappie or catfish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Use your trolling motor to stroll �¾ ounce slabs with 2 jigs tied above working best spread at least 16 inches apart. Small roadrunner type baits and small crappie jigs working. Crappie are fair and numbers are showing up in the creeks and shallow water with minnows.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are staging on secondary points hitting slow moving swimbaits, or along grass edges with chatterbaits. Dan’s Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan’s Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good scattered on main lake points and humps in 25-35 feet of water with slabs and jigs. Crappie are in 2-4 feet of water on minnows in the creek tributaries.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning on the banks hitting white spinnerbaits, and white swim jigs. Crappie are on the banks and spawned out. It is the time to wade around the stumps for crappie.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina the crappie bite is good, bluegill are fair on crickets or worms, the catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. On the lake crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 10-20 feet of water. Crappie are full of eggs and close to spawning. Black bass are fair on crankbaits and spinnerbaits in 2-8 feet of water. Bass are spawning.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with males pushing shallow out to 3 feet of water staging on rocks near the dam and cattails. Cast soft plastics worms and creature baits on a heavy line, basically rig anything weedless to target bass in the cattails. Crappie are good in shallow water. Still not seeing big female crappie but the spawn should be around the corner.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: After the sun has risen and been up around 40 minutes, look at the 30-34 feet edges of slow tapering areas for sluggish fish, presenting white or chrome, 3/4 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs to them by dropping to bottom and reeling smoothly and continuously for about five cranks. Largemouth bass continue to move shallower with the spring warm-up.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing will pick up with the rains and look for fish to move towards creeks. Bass are near creeks and docks on crankbaits and jerkbaits.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 1-6 feet of water with frogs, wacky worms, senkos, and Texas rig lizards. If the lake continues to rise, the bass will to the flooded bushes. Crappie fishing has slowed while the creeks are muddy, but as the water clears road runners and tube jigs with 1/16 ounce heads.will be productive.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be more aggressive with storms because the water is broken and clarity is disturbed. Postspawn bass are on grass flats with anything that imitates shad like swimbaits, flukes or rattle traps. Big bass can be caught on bluff walls on the main lake working towards cove entrances with creature baits.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 12 feet of water on brush piles with minnows and jigs. Bass are good in 5-6 feet of water and in 12 feet of water with crankbaits and plastic worms. Crappie are good in 1-6 feet depending on the area. Bass are good and can be expected to be great as they get closer to spawning.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in full spawn being caught from 1-13 feet of water in the creek with jigs or minnows. Black bass are good spawning in shallow water hitting white and chartreuse spinnerbaits. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are primarily suspended near the dam, but some can be found shallow and in the crappie house. There are still a few in the crappie house and in boat slips. Bass are fair with soft plastics and crankbaits in shallow water near spawning areas.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in spawn and pre-spawn mode in 3-15 feet of water hitting jigs.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are beginning to move up the rivers in shallow water in preparation for spawning. White bass are good on slabs in 20-25 feet of water. Largemouth bass are good using soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Bass should shallow on spawning beds hitting creature baits, and post spawn or staging in deeper water near spawning areas hitting soft plastics. Crappie should be spawning or staged on brush in 8-12 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 1-15 feet of water using jigs and minnow.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black Bass are fair on main lake points, and secondary points are holding fish.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good throwing moving baits and topwaters in the morning, then moving off the bank and dragging creature baits and finesse baits around cover, rocks, docks, and vegetation.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water with quite a few male bass showing back up on beds due to the full moon.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great on weightless flukes and swimbaits in perch colors. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop. Some bass are near creek mouths and a little ways in, most are along grass lines on the main lake.
reports.by: Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: A good go-to lure continues to be the white, ⅝ ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab fished with a smoking tactic by reeling it steadily up off bottom.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-20 feet of water on brush piles or downed timber on minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are transitioning to the first breakline in 6-8 feet of water hitting Texas rig worms, crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits. Look for crappie around brush and shallow banks, small wooly buggers are excellent.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are still in the weeds on plastics.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8.48 pounds are excellent on jigs, spinnerbaits and crankbaits in 3-12 feet of water. Most of the bass are in a post spawn transition. Crappie are good in the cove pockets with black and chartreuse jigs, and in brush piles out to 10-12 feet on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 10-20 feet of water on brush piles with orange and chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good in the backs of creeks, flip every stick up as there is still some spawning action.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass will be hanging tight to the trees for a week or so until the lake stabilizes. Bass protecting fry near the trees will hit a fluke, senko or swimbait.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Blue catfish are biting from crappie wall to Train Car Cove using cut bait, or on rock with cheese bait.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent using imitation shad in the morning, then switching to Carolina or Texas rigs on main lakes points as the day progresses. Bass are good in shallow water using shad or chartreuse colored running crankbaits, and watermelon or pumpkin colored soft plastics. Crappie bite is fair to slow with fish transitioning to brush piles using minnows or grubs.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with minnows, worms and topwaters. Channel catfish and bass are good in 10-20 feet of water. Crappie are spawning biting jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been good on shad colored crankbaits and spinnerbaits. Hybrids in the morning about 12-22 feet of water jigging slabs, swimbaits, minnows or shad. Crappie are in 11-21 feet of water using plastics, hair or minnows.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles 15-20 feet of water. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are scattered on the first break line with crankbaits. Early in the morning shad are spawning and bass are chasing shallow.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow with many undersized catches. Bass are good in 3-15 feet of water flipping a creature bait or jig, or throwing a spinnerbait into flooded bushes.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass have slowed, but post spawners are setting up on points in 5-7 feet of water with Carolina rigged creature baits. Crappies are shallow, catching them on edge of banks, small fish patterns like wooly buggers are a good bet. Bream are beginning to make themselves known in the shallows, wooly buggers and small poppers should bring a strike.Crappie are good in 2-13 feet on timber and around grass lines. Black crappie are on a few bridges, but fish are not loaded up yet. Black crappie are also grouping under docks on sunny afternoons.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good hitting 7 inch curly tailed or straight worms, spinnerbaits and crankbaits in less than 10 feet of water. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows on brush piles. Report by Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding.
reports.by: Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Best fishing reports are for the sand bass on slabs fished from Blue Water Shores to the area in town by the swim beach. Largemouth bass are fair to good to 7 pounds on the beds in most area creeks and sloughs. Crappie are good on minnows and small jigs fished under a cork in the backs of the creeks near docks and rip rap. Largemouth bass are hitting large minnows, or silver and white slabs. Crappie are slow and sandbags are fair on live minnows.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on buzz baits fished near timber. Crappie are good on jigs fished over brush in 8-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Black Bass will chase small streamers and top waters above and around grass. Bead heads will tempt bream and bass.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are spread out in 8-14 feet of water. Largemouth bass are starting to be consistent on docks and rip rap along with structure being caught in spinner baits and plastic worms.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good early in 10 feet of water then in 17 feet of water in the afternoon with chartreuse or silver slabs. The second wave of spawning largemouth bass and crappie should begin soon. Largemouth bass are spawning on beds. Largemouth bass are good in 1-7 feet of water with wacky worms, weightless Texas rigs, yum dingers or swim jigs. Crappie are in 10 feet or less using minnows on standing timber, brush, or deep docks.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are still in a post-spawn in 5-10 feet of water hitting crankbaits, shaky heads spinnerbaits and Carolina rigs. Crappie are transitioning to brush piles hitting minnows or jigs. Report by Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding.
reports.by: Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on soft plastics from the bank out to 12-14 feet on brush and humps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good 15-20 feet of water on brush with minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are good in flooded bushes with creature baits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-20 feet of water on brush piles with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good with a few fish on beds, but there are still plenty in the backs of pockets so use shallow moving baits like a wake bait, swimbait or frog to get some of those good ones.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Some sandies are up the creeks as well biting slabs, jigs, and live bait. Crappie are slow to fair in the main lake and creeks in 4-25 feet of water on bridge columns, brush piles, rock piles, stumps, and laydowns with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good early in 10 feet of water then in 17 feet of water in the afternoon with chartreuse or silver slabs. Expect male largemouth bass to enter protection mode as the fry are hatching. Largemouth bass are good on spawning beds in 1-4 feet of water in the creek channels using swim jigs, Texas rigs, spinnerbaits, and chatterbaits. Crappie are good fishing minnows in brush, standing timber, and creek channels in 1-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on brush piles. Largemouth bass are good in shallow water on chatterbaits, spooks, and frogs.
reports.by: Wyatt Frankens, Wyatt Frankens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good with the first signs of post-spawn bass munching on shad or junior sized jerkbaits. Crappie population is good.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair to 10 pounds. Bass are schooling mid-lake with catches to 5 pounds are being caught on top waters. Crappie still fair up both rivers on small jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good, with the fish beginning post-spawn spread out. Crappie are fair, as they spread back out, fishing the open, deeper water has been hampered by wind and storms.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great using minnows and jigs in 12 in of water on brush piles and under docks. Male crappie are starting to lay on beds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair to slow in 10-20 feet of water with live shad, small slabs and jigs white, and silver are good colors.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent with regular catches from both anglers on shore and on boats casting weightless flukes into vegetation. Crappie are good, but biting less frequently after the recent rainfall made the water turbid. Anglers are reporting success on crappie jigs with live minnows and crappie bites.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: White bass are related to humps and long points in 17-26 feet of water using 3/4 ounce slab with a jig 12 inches above. Crappie are fair and relating to brush 12-14 feet deep.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: 25-35 feet later in the day on slabs. Crappie on minnows or blue and white jigs in 10-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Best baits are a slab and jig combination for the bottom hugging fish, and if you get some top water, just about any small and shiny bait will catch fish. Crappie are fair on windblown points with shad.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catfish and crappie are fair, and bluegill are good on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black bass are fair in 5-8 feet of water hitting soft plastics and jerkbaits. Crappie are good on the main lake brush piles in 10-15 feet of water and pilings biting minnows and very small jigs.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing is excellent right now with numerous 7 and 8 pound bass being taken each week for the past several weeks in small, local tournaments. A few gulls continue to stop over as they migrate, occasionally signaling the presence of light topwater action by schoolie-sized largemouth feeding on shad on the surface.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Hybrid striper and white bass have been solid with easy limits of fish coming off artificials including swimbaits and slabs. Crappie are good on minnow and jigs in 12-15 feet on brush and timber. The largemouth bass bite is good with shallow franks, worms and spinner baits doing damage. We are seeing lily pads in several coves and bass are in them.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is good on brush piles using jigs in 14-18 feet of water. Bass fishing is good on top waters early and swim baits off the banks late morning.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with good numbers of fish being caught, but not many big fish. Crappie are fair in shallow water, with a few fish starting to show up on docks and shallow brush piles.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the main lake in shallow water and pockets, and points off the main lake with swimbaits and craws. More bass starting to show up in marinas. Bass are good on main lake flats with grass where you can use a number of techniques including shallow to medium crankbaits, swimbaits and spinnerbaits. Bass are good on small swimbaits and under spins.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in 10 feet of water on crankbaits, spinnerbaits, and trick worms. Crappie slow and scattered from the shallows to 20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Paul Taylor, The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with several 5-6.5 pound catches using a variety or lures but the lure of choice continues to be worms. Crappie anglers are catching good numbers.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: A few smaller size crappie at the house or shallow on rocks, and some have transitioned to deeper water brush piles with minnows or jigs. Bass are slow with a few late spawners shallow, but most are post spawn on chatterbaits and spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are almost done spawning. Post spawn crappie are moving back to edges of deeper water on stumps and brush. A bunch of small crappie can be caught on the river side.
reports.by: Jerry Gennings, local angler and guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be caught in spawn and pre-spawn patterns in 1-18 feet of water using jigs and minnow.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black Bass are fair on main lake points, 10-20 feet of water using Ned rigs, shaky heads, and drop shot.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be shallow on soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in all stages of the spawn. Target spawning bass on beds with your favorite bed lure. To catch pre-spawn and post-spawn bass on brush piles, cast Carolina rigs and crankbaits, or on windblown points with white jerkbaits. Crappie are fair shallow moving back to brush piles in 25 feet of water with small jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Jim Brack, Athens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been consistently shallow for the last couple of weeks.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been great on weightless flukes and swim baits in perch colors. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop.
reports.by: Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: My most successful white bass trips involved finding fish in 28-31 feet of water around mid-morning using side-imaging, spot-Locking atop these fish, then working white, 5/8 or 3/4 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs vertically with a smoking tactic in conjunction with LiveScope to gauge their response to retrieve speed until we found the sweet spot. White bass, hybrid striped bass, largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, drum, gar, and catfish are all getting in on this right now.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning shallow. Bass are hitting Texas rigs, jigs, spinnerbaits and wacky rigs. Crappie are biting minnows and jigs on brush piles or standing timber. Report by Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding.
reports.by: Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-20 feet of water on brush piles on minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are transitioning to the first breakline in 6-8 feet of water hitting Texas rig worms, crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits. Look for black bass in feeding areas, boat docks, brush and grass. Look for crappie around brush and retaining walls shallow, small wooly buggers are excellent.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass catches in the weeds on plastics.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been hit-or-miss. Slabs and swimbaits have been productive. Largemouth bass are also close to finishing their spawn.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 5.21 pounds are excellent on jigs, spinnerbaits and crankbaits in 3-8 feet of water. Most bass are in a post spawn transition with the last wave coming next full moon. Crappie are excellent in the cove pocket suspended on black and chartreuse jigs and brush piles on minnows in 10-12 feet with some fish spawning or post spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Consistent fishing patterns for catfish, crappie and bass near the restaurant, off rocks and floating docks with small minnows, worms, and cut bait. Bass are in a transition period switching to summer patterns.
reports.by: The Bait Barn

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Blue catfish are being caught in front of the crappie wall drifting or anchoring cheese bait, cut bait channel catfish on rock piles out on the lake.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent on moving baits around grass, or with a neko rig on deeper grass.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Reports of great catches using silver or white slabs and spinnerbaits and retrieving off the bottom at a very slow retrieve to catch these fish in depths of 8-16 feet of water. The crappie have also migrated back into the main lake.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent on a swimbait or crankbait around shallow rock. Bass are good in shallow water using shad or chartreuse colored running crankbaits, and watermelon or pumpkin colored soft plastics. Crappie bite is fair to slow with fish transitioning to brush piles using minnows or grubs.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Channel catfish and bass are good in 10-20 feet of water. Crappie are spawning biting jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs at the docks. Crappie shallow are good.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on soft plastics. Crappie are in 12-30 feet of water using plastics, hair or minnows.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Corpus Christi Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Captain Damian Hubbs, Top Gun Outfitters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are transitioning to the first breakline in 6-8 feet of water hitting Texas rig worms, crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on points, secondary points and in the creek channels. Crappie are slow with many catches of undersized crappie 5-15 feet of water on vertical hardwoods.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are shallow in the creeks spawning. Bass are spawning in shallow water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good to excellent on slabs and spinnerbaits fished near main lake flats from in town near the shores to the flats near Blue Water Shores. Crappie are reported as fair to good in the back of creeks on small minnows and or jigs worked under a cork. Crappie are being caught on many areas of the lake including most creeks from in town to Decordova Bend Estates. Black bass reports are fair to good in numbers with an occasional bigger fish to 7 pounds plus. Crappie are fair on jigs and small minnows fished from the bank. Largemouth bass are staying near cover, with some sizeable catches being reported.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are holding tight to structure and docks being caught on worms and grubs. Crappie are being caught in 8-14 feet of water on brush piles being caught with small plastics and hand tied jigs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair scattered between shallow water and brush in 15 feet of water hitting minnows or jigs. Sand bass are fair in main creek channels on minnows or slabs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing. Expect the bass bite to be tough after the rains.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-20 feet of water with orange and chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Some sandies are up the creeks as well biting slabs, jigs, and live bait. Crappie are slow to fair in the main lake and creeks in 4-25 feet of water on bridge columns, brush piles, rock piles, stumps, and laydowns with minnows and jigs. Bass are good from the banks out to 12 feet on crankbaits and bladed jigs. Crappie are transitioning to deeper main lake points and brush.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow catching a few along the hydrilla on spinnerbait and underspin swimbaits. Crappie are good in brush piles in 25 feet of water using minnows and larger jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good with the first signs of post-spawn bass munching on shad. Crappie population is good.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are bass good with some catches up to 13 pounds. Crappie are fair up rivers in shallow water around brush on minnows and red head jigs.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: A lot of flooded shoreline grass and brush, and some low hanging branches in the water are good for bass. Crappie are finishing the spawn and returning to deeper habitats.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie still great in shallow water minnows and jigs. Catching a lot of male crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are shallow in the grass schooled up on bait. Crappie are at the end of the spawn in shallow grass and suspended in trees along the edges and mouths creeks.
reports.by: Captain Hank Harrison, Double H Precision Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Fish in 10-20 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs white, and silver are good colors.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: White bass are relating to humps and long points in 17-26 feet of water using 3/4 ounce Bovee slab with a jig 12 inches above. Crappie are fair and relating to brush 12-14 feet deep.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are good on slabs 25-35 feet of water. Crappie are starting to show up in brush piles decent on sunny days jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Best baits are slabs for the bottom hugging fish and if you get some top water, just about any small and shiny bait. Crappie spawn is ongoing in 2-4 feet of water biting minnows.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are on points and drains in shallow water spawning, and some are in a post spawn biting crankbaits and Carolina rigs. Crappie are fair in the shallows near stumps and fair on the brush piles. Some crappie are spawning near cypress trees, wade anglers can target these. Bass are good keying on hard clay points, grass edges and flooded timber with swim jigs, chatterbaits, topwater spooks or pop-r’s. Crappie have finished spawning in 12-20 feet of water on brush piles and standing timber.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catfish and crappie are fair, and bluegill are good on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black bass are fair in 5-8 feet of water hitting soft plastics and jerkbaits. Crappie are fair on the main lake brush piles in 10-15 feet of water and pilings biting minnows and very small jigs.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good off the crappie dock with minnows. Bass are fair and the spawn should kick off after a few consecutive days of warmer weather.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing is excellent right now with numerous 7-8 pound bass being taken each week for the past several weeks in small, local tournaments. Bare, stony points in 12-19 feet worked with a 3/8 or ⅝ ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab by banging the bottom, then lifting the lure about a foot and repeating this process will produce fish 12-26 inches.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. Largemouth bass bite is great. With the shad spawn starting, look for active bass on rip rap and shallow dock posts.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth bass are good on live shad along the bluffs on the banks in 2-4 feet of water. Also fair on spooks early and look for largemouth off the banks in 6-12 feet of water on main lake points near rocks. Crappie are good on brush piles in 12-18 feet of water on jigs using electronics to locate active fish working in and out of the brush.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair from the flooded bank out to 5 feet with frogs, chatterbaits and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the main lake in shallow water and coves off the main lake with swimbaits and craws.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow but should improve in heavy cover in 8-12 feet of water with jigs or live minnows. Largemouth bass are fair on soft plastics and some topwaters.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in 10 feet of water on crankbaits and trick worms. Crappie slow in 20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Paul Taylor, The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is improving in shallow water on live minnows and artificial jigs fished around shoreline trees in the back of coves and marinas. Largemouth bass are spawning and can still be caught on Texas rigs, small swimbaits, bladed jigs and creature baits in creeks and flats.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are best with underspins on wind blown banks and yum dingers.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Some catches of smaller size crappie at the house or shallow on rocks with minnows or jigs. Bass are slow in shallow water and transitioning deeper in a post spawn using soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on the bank spawning, and scarce in deeper water. Some crappie continue to spawn along the bank, but many fish have spawned out transitioning to deeper water near major creek mouths.
reports.by: Jerry Gennings, local angler and guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie good on minnows in 1-4 feet of water and in 8-15 feet of water.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good, with numbers being caught on main and secondary points in 5-15 feet of water with senkos, wacky rigs, Texas rigged lizards, rattle traps, chatterbaits and crankbaits.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good at the state park and around the bridges.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the grass on yum dingers. Shad are running against the docks attracting the bass and white bass on jerkbaits. Bass have been consistently shallow for the last couple of weeks. Majority of the bass in the lake have spawned.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake B.A. Steinhagen fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass can be caught on Texas rigged worms and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good along grass lines in 4-10 feet of water with 4-5 inch flukes, or on main lake humps with Carolina rigs, jigging spoons and shaky heads. Some bass are on beds in the cuts. Bass are good around the reeds and grassy areas with weightless flukes and swimbaits. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Successful white bass trips involved finding fish in 28-31 feet of water around mid-morning using side-imaging, Spot-Locking atop these fish, then working white, 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs vertically with a "smoking" tactic in conjunction with LiveScope to gauge their response to retrieve speed until we found the sweet spot. White bass, hybrid striped bass, largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, drum, gar, and catfish are all getting in on this right now.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good, spawning in shallow water hitting minnows or jigs. Sand bass are good under the Texas State Highway 21 bridge hitting white or chartreuse slabs or minnows. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are transitioning to the first breakline in 6-8 feet of water hitting Texas rig worms, crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits. Look for black bass in feeding areas, boat docks, brush and grass. Look for crappie around brush and retaining walls shallow, small wooly buggers are excellent.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass can be caught in the cattails and weeds with worms and jigs.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Switch to a chartreuse slab as the fish back off into deeper water. Largemouth bass are up in the shallows. Crappie are actively spawning across the lake.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 9.30 pounds are excellent on chatterbaits, spinnerbaits and crankbaits in 3-8 feet of water. Most of the bass are spawning or post spawn. Crappie are excellent suspended in cove pockets with black and chartreuse jigs and brush piles on minnows in 10-12 feet, with some in 1-4 feet spawning.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Consistent fishing patterns for catfish, crappie and bass near the restaurant, off rocks and floating docks with small minnows, worms, and cut bait. Bass were suspended on brush piles hitting jigs.
reports.by: The Bait Barn

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 10-20 feet of water on chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: When the water level is stable bass are good with flukes, senkos, swimbaits and even some topwater action now is heating up.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent, slowly rolling a swimbait and spinnerbait along shoreline grass, or dragging a drop shot finesse worm through deeper grass.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Reports of great catched using silver or white slabs and spinners and retrieving off the bottom at a very slow retrieve to catch these fish in depths of 17-26 feet of water. The crappie have also migrated back into the main lake.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent in the mornings on a small swimbait or spinnerbaits. Black bass are good from the bank out to 10 feet of water using soft plastic worms, flukes, and chatterbaits. Crappie are good in shallow water with small jigs, grubs, or live minnows.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting jigs and minnows. Bass are biting jigs.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Catching quite a few bass at the bulkheads, but then moving 12-14 near structures. Crappie have been fair at best for this time of year. Hybrids are biting in the morning in 10-15 feet, and as the day warms in 15-25 jigging slabs, swimbaits or minnows and shad.
reports.by: Brad Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in shallow water near boat houses in 2-6 feet of water with minnows or jigs. Sand bass are good on main lake points in 15-25 feet of water with yellow or chartreuse slabs or trolling. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are transitioning to the first breakline in 6-8 feet of water hitting Texas rig worms, crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good on main lake structures with slabs and cohos. Crappie are good shallow and mid depths on jigs.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the reeds, timber and back of coves in 4-8 feet of water with flukes, Texas rigged worms, creature baits, and shallow crankbaits.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Offshore bass are good on humps and points in 5-7 feet of water with Carolina rigs with light weights, mid-running crankbaits, and shaky heads. First phase bass spawners are now in a post spawn pattern and aggressive. Crappies are shallow, small fish patterns like wooly buggers are a good bet. Crappie are great with some pre-spawn fish, some fish actively spawning and some post spawn. All crappie on Lake Fork do not go shallow to spawn and we catch fish in 18-20 feet that are spawning on timber. It is a very versatile time to catch crappie with multiple patterns. Minnows will work great right now but any crappie baits will catch fish.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good hitting 7 inch curly tailed or straight worms, spinnerbaits and crankbaits in less than 10 feet of water. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows. Report by Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding.
reports.by: Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are shallow in the creeks spawning. Bass are shallow as well.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie angling is reported as good in the backs of creeks on small minnows and jigs worked under a cork in 2-7 feet of water. White bass are fair to good on humps and ridges on slabs and small minnows. Largemouth bass are good to 7 pounds on the beds using soft plastics and spinnerbaits. Some good largemouth bass are reported working the laydowns in the river above Granbury.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Later in the day move deeper with slabs. Bass can be caught from the bank along the riprap near boat ramps. Crappie are related to rocky outcroppings and rock structure.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are tight to structure in 8-14 feet of water and pink jigs seems to be the ticket. Largemouth bass are being caught consistently on top waters and will only get better with time.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water on soft plastics, as well as on brush out to 14 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great shallow in the grass with jerkbaits, Texas rigged soft plastics. Crappie are biting minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Black crappie are post spawn in 15-20 feet of water on brush piles hitting minnows or jigs. White crappie are spawning in the shallows with minnows or jigs. Sand bass are good in main creek channels 20-30 feet deep on slabs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing. Expect the bass bite to be tough after the rains.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 3-15 feet of water in the middle of the spawn. So next time you come into the cove, you can hit all the threaded trees because a male Crappie will replace the one you caught in the previous day. White 1 ounce RSR lures slabs working great. Tying a jig 18 inches above the slab will sometimes produce two fish per drop. Some pre-spawn black bass males are in 3-15 feet of water hitting 3-6 foot divers, Texas rig worms, and creature baits. Some bass are on brush piles biting swimbaits and smaller Alabama rigs.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-20 feet of water with orange and chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good near the mouths of creeks, coves or flipping docks with wacky worms, Texas rigs, finesse baits, and jigs.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Some sandies are up the creeks as well biting slabs, jigs, and live bait. Crappie are slow to fair in the main lake and creeks in 4-25 feet of water on bridge columns, brush piles, rock piles, stumps, and laydowns with minnows and jigs. Crappie are fair on live minnows and hair jigs as fish move shallow to spawn. White bass and hybrid bass are chasing bait on the main lake and going into the creeks hitting shad, slabs, imitation shad and paddle tail swimbaits. Largemouth bass are from the bank to 6 feet of water on spinnerbaits, lipless crankbaits, squarebill crankbaits or any type of soft plastics.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Expect male largemouth bass to enter protection mode as the fry are hatching. Largemouth bass are good on spawning beds in 1-4 feet of water in the creek channels using swim jigs, Texas rigs, spinnerbaits, and chatterbaits. Crappie are good fishing minnows in brush, standing timber, and creek channels in 1-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair off points and along the hydrilla with Texas rigged worms using watermelon red and redbug. Crappie are good to excellent with Bobby Garland jigs and minnows fishing brush piles in 20-25 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is improving with the first signs of post-spawn bass munching on shad. Crappie population is good.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on red chatterbaits flipping soft plastics in the reeds in 1-3 feet of water. Look for spawning bass shallow. Crappie are good around boat docks on chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good and in all phases of the spawn. Bass are being caught on rage craws or bugs in white or green pumpkin. Crappie are fair on minnows and small jigs in the back of shallow pockets and coves.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are steady on squarebill crankbaits and small swimbaits. Crappie and catfish are slow.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still good in the shallows next to reeds, but may be completing their spawn and starting to move to their deeper habitat.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
