reports.text: Crappie are biting in shallow water off the bank.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are shallow in the grass schooled up on bait. Crappie are at the end of the spawn in shallow grass and suspended in trees along the edges and mouth creeks.
reports.by: Captain Hank Harrison, Double H Precision Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are slow to fair in 2-20 feet of water with live shad, small slabs and jigs.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair relating to brush 12-14 feet of water.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good on slabs and live shad in 25-35 feet of water. Crappie are good in 5-15 feet of water using minnows or jigs.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Best baits are Slabs for the bottom hugging fish and if you get some top water, just about any small and shiny bait. Reports of crappie in 2-4 feet of water biting minnows.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning in the grass lines in 4-15 feet of water biting crankbaits. Crappie bite is good in the shallows and slow on the brush piles. Some crappie are spawning near cypress trees, wade anglers can target these. Bass are good keying on hard clay points, grass edges and flooded timber with swim jigs, chatterbaits, topwater spooks or pop-r’s. Crappie have finished spawning in 12-20 feet of water on brush piles and standing timber.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catfish and crappie are fair, and bluegill are good on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black bass are fair in 3-6 feet of water hitting spinnerbaits, and crankbaits. Crappie are fair on the main lake brush piles in 14 feet of water and pilings biting minnows and very small jigs.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been caught using square bill crankbaits in shad patterns.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good off the crappie dock with minnows. Bass are fair with several smaller fish being caught. Bass are bedding, when you can find fish cast soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing is excellent right now with numerous 7-8 pound bass being taken each week for the past several weeks in small, local tournaments. Bare, stony points in 12-19 feet of water with a 3/8 or ⅝ ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab by banging the bottom, then lifting the lure about a foot and repeating this process will produce fish 12-26 inches.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Fish have been feeding on large groups of threadfin shad and swimbaits and slabs are working. The crappie have been good in shallow water on warm days. The largemouth bite has been good.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and catfish are slow. The bass bite is good north of the U.S.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is improving under docks and on submerged structures using electronics to locate active fish. Some crappie are still in the creeks and on structures and lay downs in 2-5 feet of water. Bass are good on live shad along the bluffs off the banks in 5-10 feet of water. Expect the topwater and slab bite to heat up soon.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair but many smaller fish are getting to the bait before the bigger fish because the water is warm. Crappie fishing has been hit-and-miss while fish are spawning and post-spawn.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the grass and on main lakes flats in 4-12 feet of water, or in the cuts and coves with shaky heads, dropshots, and shallow to medium diving crankbaits. Some catfish are mixed in with the bass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 10 feet of water crankbaits and spinnerbaits, and trick worms. Crappie good on brush piles with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Paul Taylor, The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with Alabama rigs, jerkbaits, flukes, and Yum Dingers. Bass are great with more and more bedding bass showing up. Crappie are good in 10-15 feet of water with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Some catches of smaller size crappie at the house or shallow on rocks with minnows or jigs. Bass are slow to fair with a few on spawning beds using soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Welsh fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with Texas rigged worms, and chatterbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good on main lake structures with slabs and cohos. Crappie are good shallow and mid depths on jigs.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on the bank spawning, and scarce in deeper water. Wade fishing can be done effectively for crappie.
reports.by: Jerry Gennings, local angler and guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie good on minnows in 15-25 feet of water.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair in 10-20 feet of water on main lake points and secondary points near deep water access using rattle traps, crankbaits, underspins, Texas rigged lizards and jerkbaits.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are shallow. Bass should be spawning.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is good at the dam and around the bridges on black and chartreuse jigs. Some crappie are post spawn.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in all stages of the spawn. Target spawning bass on beds with your favorite bed lure. To catch pre-spawn and post-spawn bass on brush piles cast Carolina rigs and crankbaits, or on windblown points with white jerkbaits. Crappie are shallow moving back to brush piles in 20 feet of water with small jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Jim Brack, Athens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good throwing flukes, spinnerbaits and worms around the grass lines. Work the edges of coves off the reeds for big bedding bass with a fluke or lizard. Bass have been good on watermelon seed flukes and watermelon red pearls around thin reeds. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Move to 24-32 feet and work white ⅝ ounce or 3/4 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs by cranking them up off the bottom for 5 cranks at a moderate speed.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair scattered in 2-20 feet of water biting minnows or jigs. Sand bass are excellent under the Texas State Highway 21 bridge hitting white or chartreuse slabs or minnows. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are on spawning beds in shallow water. Look for black bass on nests in creeks and in protected coves. Look for crappie around brush and retaining walls shallow, small wooly buggers are excellent.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are very good up to 7 pounds on rocks with crankbaits, chatterbaits and senkos. Crappie are good in the marina or around hardwood main lake or creek entrance.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8.08 pounds are excellent on jerkbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits and crankbaits in 3-8 feet of water. Bass are in all stages of the spawn. Crappie are excellent suspended in cove pockets on black and chartreuse jigs, or on brush piles with minnows in 10-12 feet of water. Some crappie are starting to spawn in 1-4 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to spawn and if in the right area, many catches can be had flipping trees in 2-5 feet of water. Crappie continue to be good in 2-12 feet of water on chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the morning along rocky banks with a spinnerbait.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Reports of great catches in 17-26 feet of water using silver or white slabs and spinnerbaits with a very slow retrieve off the bottom. Crappie have also migrated back into the main lake.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good from the bank out to 10 feet of water using soft plastic worms, flukes, and chatterbaits. Crappie are good in shallow water with small jigs, grubs, or live minnows.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie, bass, sand bass and channel catfish are good on worms and minnows.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on beds with some big gals being caught. Crappie are fair.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 2-6 feet of water around boat houses with minnows or jigs. Sand bass are good on main lake points in 10-20 feet of water with yellow or chartreuse slabs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are on spawning beds in shallow water.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 3-8 feet of water flipping bushes and hardwoods on soft plastics, chatterbaits and spinnerbaits. Crappie are fair in hardwoods in 3 feet of water with minnows on a slip cork.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is improving everyday, especially along windy banks. Bass are nesting and under lots of fishing pressure. Crappies are shallow, small fish patterns like wooly buggers are a good bet. Lake Fork crappie fishing is heating up like the water temperature this week.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving to the creeks to spawn. Bass are moving up shallower to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie action is improving in the backs of creeks, but many are still in transition to the spawning grounds. The best crappie action is reported in the river north of Granbury, or in town near subdivision creek entrances. Largemouth bass are moving to their spawning beds in the back of the creeks and sloughs and are good on soft plastics and spinnerbaits. White bass are schooled up on humps and ridges and are good on slabs and spinnerbaits worked vertically. The crappie are still very active and hitting on small to medium minnows fishing from the shore, or using light colored jigs around docks. Sand bass are picking up on minnows, slabs and swimbaits in various colors. Largemouth bass are…
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on white spinnerbaits fished in very shallow water. Crappie are good in shallow coves and ditches all over the lake.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught from the bank along the riprap near boat ramps. Crappie are related to rocky outcroppings and rock structure.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Bait fish patterns above the grass should work for cruising bass and pickerel. Look for bedding bass in the grass and shallow brush.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are spawning and could possibly be done soon. Crappie are in 3-12 feet of water on structure and in the mud biting hands tied jigs, small plastics and minnows. Largemouth bass are staying in docks and riprap biting swimbaits and worms rigged lightly.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are still in a post-spawn in 5-10 feet of water hitting crankbaits, shaky heads spinnerbaits and Carolina rigs. Crappie are up the creeks on minnows or jigs. Report by Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding. Crappie are slow to fair.
reports.by: Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good from the bank to 8 feet of water on worms and creature baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good within 2-6 feet of water biting on minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are on spawning beds in shallow water.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 3-15 feet of water with some setting up on spawning beds. Some pre-spawn black bass males are in 3-5 feet of water hitting 3-6 foot divers, Texas rig worms, and creature baits. Some bass are on brush piles biting swimbaits and smaller Alabama rigs.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 4-12 feet of water with orange and chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Numbers of bass have finished spawning, but bass are still in creek mouths and flats around the grass patches. Work chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, wake baits and underspin swimbaits will catch these bass. Target bedding bass with lizards, worms, fluke or a jig.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Some sandies are up the creeks as well biting slabs, jigs, and live bait. Crappie are fair to good in the main lake and creeks in 4-32 feet of water on bridge columns, brush piles, rock piles, stumps, and laydowns with minnows and jigs. Crappie are fair on live minnows and hair jigs as fish move shallow to spawn. White bass and hybrid bass are chasing bait on the main lake and going into the creeks hitting shad, slabs, imitation shad and paddle tail swimbaits. Largemouth bass are from the bank to 6 feet of water on spinnerbaits, lipless crankbaits, squarebill crankbaits or any type of soft plastics.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in the hydrilla on gold jerkbaits and wacky rigged worms. Crappie are good fishing brush piles in 20-25 feet on minnows and Bobby Garland jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good on minnows and artificials. Crappie are fair on artificial baits and minnows. White bass are good on minnows, slabs, or any vertical presentations.
reports.by: Kenneth Wysong, SharKens Honey Hole

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Many Naconiche bass bed deeper than most other East Texas lakes. Crappie population is good.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on spawning beds in out to 2 feet of water with black and chartreuse jigs. Largemouth bass are fair on Carolina rigged worms and lizards near spawning beds.
reports.by: Clay Major, Major Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in all phases of spawn in 2-10 feet of water. Crappie are good in shallow water on red head jigs with green, and limits can be caught on minnows.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in the shallows and in the deeper lake cover and shelter. Bass are improving in shallow nesting areas and immediate shelter and staging area fishing remains good.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting great on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are the end of the spawn so expect fish to begin schooling to heavily chase bait. Bass can be caught on topwater baits, chatterbaits, weightless fluke, and swimbaits.
reports.by: Captain Hank Harrison, Double H Precision Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair in 2-20 feet of water with live shad, small slabs and jigs.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, hybrids and crappie are fair to good on the banks and near the dam. Largemouth bass can be caught on soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Fish are related closer to the bottom more than suspended using slab jig combination. Crappie are fair in shallow water 1-3 feet by the reeds and golf-coarse and are moving in and out of shallow water for spawning, relating to brush in 12-14 feet of water.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Best baits are slabs for the bottom hugging fish. Reports of crappie in 2-4 feet of water biting minnows.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning in the grass lines in 4-15 feet of water biting crankbaits. Crappie are slow with fish scattered from shallow water to brush piles. Some crappie are spawning near cypress trees, wade anglers can target these. Bass can still be found shallow but the majority of the numbers and size are 10-22 feet deep staging on secondary and main lake points and ledges.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, crappie, and bluegill are good on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black bass are fair in 3-6 feet of water hitting spinnerbaits, and crankbaits. Crappie are fair on the main lake brush piles in 14 feet of water and pilings biting minnows and very small jigs.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good near the dam with a jig on slip cork, or in 3 feet of water in coves. Bass are fair with a few caught by anglers targeting crappie. When you find bass on beds, cast soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing is improving as new hydrilla begins to grow and the lake warms toward preferred spawning temperatures bringing many fish up shallow. Target bare, stony points in 12-19 feet of water worked with a 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab by banging the bottom, then lifting the lure about a foot and repeating this process will produce fish 12-26 inches.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush in 10-15 feet of water and some in the creeks 3-10 feet of water on warmer days. Bass are fair on hard baits in the backs of the coves and creeks on warmer days. Plastics off the main lake points in 5-15 feet of water and we are catching smallmouth on live shad along the bluffs really well.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is fair while fish are between stages. Lots of bass have spawned, and more are coming in to spawn. Bass are shallow and the best baits have been slowly fishing a Wacky worm or Texas rigged lizards.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good around and in coves lining the shorelines and in deeper water.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in 3-5 feet of water using jigs or live minnows.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: The shallow crappie bite is picking up as the water temperatures continue to rise and fish spawn. Largemouth bass are spawning and can still be caught on Texas rigs, small swimbaits, bladed jigs and creature baits in creeks and flats.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Finding numbers of bass, but fish over 5 pounds have been hard to find. Bass are great with more and more bedding bass showing up. Quality bass can be quite easy to catch in numbers using 4 or 5 inch worms are best, but spinnerbaits and swimbaits will also land catches.
reports.by: David Report by David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Some catches of smaller size crappie at the house or shallow on rocks with minnows or jigs. Bass are slow with a few on spawning beds using soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow using minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are scattered in shallow water, with some beginning to move out of shallow water to timber and brush on edges of creeks and river. These next couple weeks should be the main spawn for crappie now that water temperatures are rising above 65 degrees. Crappie and catfish are good below the dam.
reports.by: Jerry Gennings, local angler and guide
